title: Citigroup Stock Slips 4% Despite an Earnings Beat. Here’s What the Market Is Missing
detail:
Citigroup Stock Slips 4% Despite an Earnings Beat. Here’s What the Market Is Missing
Gian Estrada
Tue, October 13, 2026 at 1:15 PM MDT 4 min read
C
Trade C on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
Citigroup Stock Slips 4% Despite an Earnings Beat. Here's What the Market Is Missing ©Warchi from Getty Images Signature and Tanakorn Akkarakulchai from Getty Images via Canva

Citigroup (C:NYSE) beat Wall Street's estimates on Tuesday, October 13, and the stock fell anyway. Citi reported third-quarter net income of $5.25 billion, or $2.85 a share, above the $2.66 analysts expected, according to LSEG data cited by Reuters. Revenue rose 8% to $23.8 billion. Shares were down about 3.8%, trading near $127 during Tuesday's session.

It's the second quarter in a row that a beat met a selloff. Citi's Q2 results drew a 5% drop in July.

Citi's Steadiest Businesses Carried the Quarter

Services and Wealth led revenue growth, supported by both net interest income and fees. Services revenue rose 15% to $6.6 billion, and Wealth also grew 15%, to $3.3 billion. CEO Jane Fraser said Services had "momentum in every driver."

Trading went the other way. Markets revenue fell to $6.1 billion from $7.0 billion in the second quarter, a 13% sequential drop, though it was still up 6% from a year earlier. Equities did most of the damage, sliding from $2.3 billion to $1.7 billion.

What TIKR Data Shows About Citi's Mix
C Quarterly Services, Wealth and Markets Revenue (TIKR)

The chart shows two very different businesses. Services climbed from $5.02 billion in the September 2024 quarter to $6.38 billion in June 2026, up 27%, and dipped only once along the way. Markets swung between $4.54 billion and $7.25 billion, a high-to-low gap of 60%.

In the third quarter, Services and Wealth together brought in about $9.9 billion, roughly 1.6 times what Markets earned.

The Returns and Outlook Behind the Beat

Returns went backward from Q2. Return on tangible common equity fell to 11.5% from 13.0%, and management told analysts to expect Markets revenue to drop about 20% from the third quarter, "possibly a bit more." On $6.1 billion, that points to under $5 billion in the fourth quarter.

C, BAC and JPM Stock NTM P/E (TIKR)

The multiple also shows the market has already paid for some of the turnaround. Citi trades at 11.40 times forward earnings, above its three-year average of 10.43 times and level with Bank of America (BAC:NYSE) at 11.27 times. JPMorgan (JPM:NYSE) still gets 13.65 times, a premium of about 20% to Citi.

Does Citi Need a Re-Rating to Work?
C Stock Valuation Model Results (TIKR)

I built my model to answer that, so I gave Citi no credit for one. I have the P/E shrinking about 2% a year, revenue growing 4.1% a year, below this quarter's 8% growth, with management expecting a seasonal decline in Markets revenue in Q4), and the net income margin reaching 21.5%, up from 14.9% last year as management pushes toward its 11% to 13% return targets.

That gets Citi to about $179 by the end of 2030, a 36% gain from the $132 it closed at before earnings, or 7.6% a year. After Tuesday's drop, the gap to the target is closer to 41%. It's a respectable return built entirely on earnings growth, and it lines up with the $179 in TIKR's October 5 preview. The quarter didn't change the math.

Key Points

Interested in Citigroup Inc.? Here are five stocks we like better.

Citigroup reported strong third-quarter results: Net income rose 17% to $5.2 billion, revenue increased 8% to $23.8 billion, and ROTCE reached 11.5%. Management expects to exceed its 2026 ROTCE target and projects full-year ROTCE above 11%.

Services and Wealth led business growth, with revenue rising 15% in each division. Markets revenue grew 6%, while Banking revenue increased 6%, supported by a 77% surge in equity capital markets revenue.

Citi returned more than $4 billion to shareholders, including $3 billion in buybacks and a 12% dividend increase. The bank also advanced its Banamex exit, with deconsolidation expected in 2027, and said AI initiatives are producing benefits that exceed related investments.

Ag Equipment's Recovery Trade Meets Washington's Scrutiny

Citigroup (NYSE:C) reported third-quarter 2026 net income of $5.2 billion, or $2.85 per share, as revenue rose 8% year over year to $23.8 billion. The bank generated a return on tangible common equity, or ROTCE, of 11.5%, up 180 basis points from a year earlier, while net income increased 17%.

Chief Executive Officer Jane Fraser said the company delivered its best third-quarter revenue in a decade, with growth in four of its five businesses. Expenses were $14 billion, down 2% on a reported basis. Excluding a $726 million Banamex goodwill impairment recorded in the prior-year quarter, expenses increased 3% as Citi pulled forward certain planned investments and severance costs.

Salesforce Just Got a Rare Double Upgrade—What Changed?

"Our overall performance continues to demonstrate the disciplined and consistent execution of our strategy," Fraser said. She added that Citi expects to exceed its 2026 ROTCE target range of 10% to 11%, while continuing investments intended to support a near-term target of 11% to 13% and a longer-term goal of 14% to 15%.

Services, Wealth Lead Revenue Growth

Services posted a 15% increase in revenue, supported by growth in deposits, commercial card spending, trade loans and cross-border activity. Net interest income in the division rose 17%, while non-interest revenue increased 12%. Average deposits climbed 16% and average loans rose 14%.

title: JPMorgan vs. Citigroup: Which Big Bank Stock Is the Better Buy After Q3 Earnings?
detail:
JPMorgan vs. Citigroup: Which Big Bank Stock Is the Better Buy After Q3 Earnings?
Shaun Pruitt
Tue, October 13, 2026 at 1:01 PM MDT 4 min read
JPM
C
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Banking giants JPMorgan Chase JPM) and Citigroup C) kicked off third-quarter earnings season on Tuesday, delivering contrasting results amid an uncertain economic environment.

JPMorgan maintained its position as the industry leader in profitability and financial strength, despite a rare earnings miss. Meanwhile, Citigroup delivered impressive earnings growth as its multiyear restructuring efforts gained traction.

With both banks benefiting from stronger net interest income (NII), which stock offers investors the better opportunity following Q3 earnings?

JPMorgan vs. Citigroup: Q3 Results and Outlook

JPMorgan reported adjusted Q3 earnings of $5.75 per share, missing the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $5.94 by 3% despite increasing 13% from EPS of $5.07 in the prior-year quarter.

Reported revenue rose 8% year over year to $50.17 billion but also fell short of expectations of $52.2 billion. Nevertheless, trading revenue surged 15%, investment banking revenue increased 15%, and NII climbed 13% to $27.1 billion.

Encouragingly, JPMorgan raised its full-year NII outlook to $106.2 billion from $105.5 billion, while increasing its adjusted expense forecast to $108.6 billion from $107.5 billion.

Looking ahead to 2027, JPMorgan's preliminary outlook calls for NII excluding its Markets trading division of approximately $107 billion, supported by balance sheet growth and elevated interest rates.

CEO Jamie Dimon described the U.S. economy as solid, supported by resilient consumer spending and business investment, but cautioned that persistent inflation, rising interest rates, fiscal deficits, and geopolitical uncertainty remain potential headwinds.

Zacks Investment Research

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

As for Citigroup, it surpassed earnings expectations, posting adjusted Q3 EPS of $2.85, topping the Zacks EPS Consensus of $2.66 by 7% and increasing 27% from $2.24 per share a year ago.

Revenue increased 8% to $23.85 billion, also surpassing forecasts of $23.66 billion, while NII surged 14% to nearly $17 billion. Notably, Citi's services revenue climbed 15%, equities revenue increased 14%, and wealth management continued to improve.

CEO Jane Fraser highlighted positive operating leverage and accelerating returns as evidence that the company's restructuring strategy is working. Citigroup now expects to exceed its 2026 return target, while working toward a return on tangible common equity of 11%-13% in 2027-2028 and 14%-15% over the longer term.

Furthermore, Citigroup raised its full-year NII growth outlook, now expecting NII excluding markets trading to increase in the mid-to-high 6% range, up from its previous forecast of 5%-6%

title: Big banks show clean credit, but investors fear what comes next
detail:
Big banks show clean credit, but investors fear what comes next
Proactive
Tue, October 13, 2026 at 11:55 AM MDT 3 min read
JPM
C
CMC
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Wall Street's biggest banks reported no sign of credit strain in the third quarter, yet shares of retail-heavy lenders JPMorgan Chase & Co (NYSE:JPM, XETRA:CMC) and Citigroup Inc (NYSE:C) struggled Tuesday as investors looked ahead to what a flattening yield curve could mean for future credit risk.

Kathleen Brooks, research director at XTB, said none of the major banks flagged rising loan losses or credit problems. Long-end yields rising faster than short-term yields, however, is typically a sign credit risks will increase later.

"Investors tend to price this in ahead of time," Brooks said. "Although their results were solid today, it's tomorrow that investors are fearful of."

Credit metrics were a highlight. Provisions for credit losses fell 19% from a year ago to $2.74 billion, and net charge-offs of $2.2 billion were down more than $300 million. Net reserves rose by $539 million. Brooks said the figures point to low levels of bad credit and a strong financial position.

Analysts were more measured on the earnings themselves. Jefferies called JPMorgan's quarter mixed. Average loans rose 10% and deposits 8% from a year ago, while investment banking fees climbed 14%. Equities revenue of $4.95 billion beat the $4.43 billion consensus, but fixed income revenue of $5.37 billion missed the $5.95 billion estimate.

Management raised its 2026 net interest income outlook and projected $107 billion of net interest income excluding Markets in 2027, against $103 billion expected by the market. Jefferies said that should be positive for the stock.

Goldman Sachs Group Inc (NYSE:GS, XETRA:GOS) beat on investment banking, with revenue up 21% from a year ago to $3.2 billion and advisory the largest outperformer. Equities beat consensus by $1.3 billion on record financing revenue. Asset and wealth management revenue reached $5.1 billion, lifted by incentive fees, and assets under supervision hit a record $4.10 trillion.

Return on tangible common equity was 20.5%, which Jefferies said was solid but slightly less capital efficient.

Wells Fargo & Co (NYSE:WFC, XETRA:NWT)'s net interest margin held flat at 2.43%. Jefferies called the quarter mixed, as core earnings per share fell short on weaker fees and Markets net interest income. Management introduced fourth-quarter net interest income guidance of $13 billion, above Jefferies' $12.8 billion estimate.

Citigroup fared better in Jefferies' view. The analysts called its quarter positive, with net interest income of $16.98 billion topping the $16.65 billion consensus, expenses came in below estimates, and credit was better than expected. Citi raised its quarterly dividend 12% to $0.67 and lifted its full-year guidance.

For now, the quarter's results were solid, but as Brooks put it, it is what comes next that has investors on edge. They won't have long to wait, as Morgan Stanley (NYSE:MS), Bank of America Corp (NYSE:BAC) and BlackRock Inc (NYSE:BLK) are all due to report Wednesday morning.
